chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him: A man and a woman, upon whom the house collapsed, so they both died. He said: The man inherits from the woman, and the woman inherits from the man.

I said: Indeed, Abu Hanifa has introduced something regarding this. He said: And what has he introduced regarding them? I said: Two men, brothers, non-Arabs, not having any inheritor except their masters. One of them had a hundred thousand Dirhams, well known, and the other had nothing. They both sailed in a ship, so it drowned. So the one hundred thousand were extracted. What should be done with it?
He said: It should be handed over to the master of the one who had nothing.

He said: I do not deny what he has introduced in it as true, and it is like this. Then he said: Hand over the wealth to the master of the one who had nothing, and there would not be anything for the man who had wealth, to be inherited by the other master. So there is nothing for his inheritors.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on inheritance when a man and woman die simultaneously in an accident?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudence of simultaneous death (tadamun), specifically addressing the inheritance of 'mawalis' (clients) when two non-Arab brothers perish together with disparate estates. It highlights a nuanced ruling where the wealthier brother's estate passes to the master of the poorer brother, a view the Imam validates as correct, contrasting it with other schools like Abu Hanifa's. This establishes the principle that in the absence of direct heirs, the mawalis of the heir-less brother inherit the estate of the brother who had wealth but no heirs to receive it.
